scope: feature branch 030-geospatial-locations vs origin/main (git diff origin/main...HEAD excluding specs/, 139 files): correctness and spec-compliance lens with the documentation pass. Changed names searched across the checkout: Point (0 live references; 1 historical migration, 1 changelog entry), PointFactory (0; changelog only), bbox / Dataset.bbox (0 code references; 1 test asserting absence, 3 doc mentions of the removal), bbox_for_dataset (0; changelog), FAIRDM_CRS / FAIRDM_X_COORD / FAIRDM_Y_COORD (0 in code; 2 in docs and changelog naming the removal), location page and /location/<lon>/<lat>/ (0 routes; 0 template links), location_id / location.latitude / location.longitude / location__x (0 live references), Contributor.location (3 Organization-only uses read and correct), declare_addressing (1 definition, 1 doc page, 0 callers, 0 tests). 4262 tests passed and 7 skipped across the location, import/export, API, collection-table, measurement, sample, project, dataset and contributors suites, run locally on PostGIS. 207 added test functions were swept (about 160 read line by line, the rest by name and sampled assertions: API location section, organization profile form, dataset model coverage).

findings.claim: A projected point that converts to a latitude or longitude outside WGS 84's range is stored, not refused. FR-008 and the spec edge case say it must be refused. The only range guard after conversion is the GDAL transform failing outright.
findings.evidence: fairdm/contrib/location/forms.py:331-345 (read_point): after point.transform(WGS84) the only handler is `except GDALException`; there is no check that -90 <= y <= 90 and -180 <= x <= 180 on the converted point. Probe run on this branch: LocationField().compress(["4087", "20000000", "0", None, None]) (EPSG:4087 World Equidistant Cylindrical, northing 20,000,000 m, easting 0) returns Location(point=(0.0, 179.6630568239043), srid 4326), and RockSampleFactory(location=that point) stores and reads back y=179.66. The only test of the refusal, tests/test_contrib/test_location/test_forms.py `test_a_projected_point_outside_the_systems_area_is_refused` (and the matching parametrized case in tests/test_core/test_sample/test_forms.py), uses EPSG:25832 with easting 30,000,000, which PROJ rejects outright, so it exercises the GDAL-failure path and never the out-of-range-result path.
findings.reproduction: Sample form or import file: reference system 4087, northing 20000000, easting 0. Form is valid, the sample is saved at latitude 179.66; the page, the API (`coordinates: [0, 179.66]`) and every lookup then carry a latitude no WGS 84 point has. The import path shares LocationField.compress, so a file row does the same.
findings.suggested_fix: In read_point, after the transform, refuse (code out_of_range, same message as the GDAL failure) when abs(point.y) > 90 or abs(point.x) > 180. Add a test that cleans ("4087", "20000000", "0") and expects out_of_range; it must go red when the range check is removed.

findings.claim: Tabular import stores NaN and infinite elevations and NaN uncertainties. The form rejects them, the import path does not, and one such row makes the record unrenderable in the API.
findings.evidence: fairdm/contrib/location/resources.py:10-20 (MeasureWidget is a FloatWidget, whose clean() is float(value), so 'nan' and 'inf' pass) and :172-200 (set_location hands instance.location_elevation / location_uncertainty to LocationField.compress, which only tests `uncertainty < 0`, false for NaN). Django's FloatField would refuse these on the form; the import bypasses that. Probe through the real sample resource on PostGIS: rows with location_elevation 'nan', location_uncertainty 'nan' and location_elevation 'inf' all import as `new`, and read back as elevation nan, uncertainty nan, elevation inf. The database check constraint accepts NaN (PostgreSQL orders NaN above every number). rest_framework's JSONRenderer (STRICT_JSON default True, not overridden in settings) raises `ValueError: Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan` for the GeoJSON coordinates [x, y, nan] and for location_uncertainty.
findings.reproduction: Import a CSV whose location_elevation cell reads `nan` (what `str()` of a pandas NaN or a spreadsheet #N/A export writes) next to valid latitude and longitude. The row is saved. GET the API list for that sample type: the response fails to render for every page that contains the record.
findings.suggested_fix: In MeasureWidget.clean (or set_location), refuse a value for which math.isfinite is false, raising ValueError with a message naming the cell, so the row is reported and not saved. Test: a row with location_elevation 'nan' and one with location_uncertainty 'inf' are invalid rows and not saved; it must go red when the isfinite check is removed.

findings.claim: A registration that lists no fields (the documented default) gets three location inputs: the location widget plus plain location_elevation and location_uncertainty fields, and the widget's elevation and uncertainty inputs have the same names as those plain fields.
findings.evidence: fairdm/utils/inspection.py:147-170 (get_default_fields takes every editable field, so location, location_elevation and location_uncertainty are all defaults) with fairdm/contrib/location/forms.py:363-378 (LocationFormMixin.__init__ replaces `location` only). Probe: ModelConfiguration(model=RockSample).get_form_class().base_fields has ['location', 'location_elevation', 'location_uncertainty']. LocationWidget names its parts `location_elevation` and `location_uncertainty` (location.html), exactly the plain fields' input names, so a page renders two inputs of each name and id. A browser posts both and QueryDict keeps the last, so an elevation typed into the widget is overwritten by the empty plain field. Registrations with no `fields` are shown in docs/portal-development/using_the_registry.md (XRFMeasurementConfig, AdvancedMeasurementConfig) and demo CustomSampleConfig is built on that auto-detection.
findings.reproduction: Register a sample type with `class MyConfig(ModelConfiguration): model = MySample` and open its edit page: two Elevation and two Uncertainty inputs with duplicate ids. Type an elevation in the first and save: the later empty input wins and the elevation is stored as null.
findings.suggested_fix: In LocationFormMixin.__init__, when `location` is swapped, pop `location_elevation` and `location_uncertainty` from self.fields (the widget owns them). Test: a form built from a ModelConfiguration with no fields has exactly one input named location_elevation and saves an elevation typed in the widget; it must go red when the pop is removed.

findings.claim: `inside()` given a (west, south, east, north) box with west > east, which is the shape spatial_coverage returns across the 180th meridian, builds a polygon that covers the complement and returns the wrong records without an error.
findings.evidence: fairdm/contrib/location/managers.py:33 `Polygon.from_bbox(tuple(area))`. Coverage is the same (west, south, east, north) tuple and has west > east when it crosses (coverage.py, docs/portal-development/locations.md:234-240). Probe on PostGIS: samples at (178, -15) and (0, -15); Sample.objects.inside((175, -20, -175, -10)) returns the sample at longitude 0 and not the one at 178. GEOS: Polygon.from_bbox((175,-20,-175,-10)) is valid with area 3500 square degrees against the intended 100.
findings.reproduction: Sample.objects.inside(tuple(dataset.spatial_coverage(user))) for a dataset spanning the dateline returns samples across the rest of the globe and misses those in the box. Same for any dateline-crossing map extent from #497.
findings.suggested_fix: In Spatial.polygon, when a tuple has west > east, build the area as the union of (west, south, 180, north) and (-180, south, east, north), or refuse it with a ValueError that says a box across the 180th meridian is passed as a polygon. Test: the sample at 178 is inside and the one at 0 is not, for (175, -20, -175, -10); it must go red when the west > east branch is removed.

findings.claim: FR-018/FR-021 for coverage (a measurement counts at its effective location) is not demonstrated: replacing the measurement pair's `effective_location` with `location` in Dataset.spatial_coverage and Project.spatial_coverage leaves every test green.
findings.evidence: fairdm/core/dataset/models.py:407-409 and fairdm/core/project/models.py:224-226. tests/test_core/test_dataset/test_models.py TestDatasetSpatialCoverage: `test_a_measurement_with_none_is_placed_by_its_sample` puts the measurement's sample at the same point as the expected box, so the box is identical when the measurement contributes nothing; `test_a_measurement_placed_only_by_a_hidden_sample_adds_nothing` expects None, which the mutant also gives; the remaining measurement tests give the measurement its own location. tests/test_contrib/test_location/test_coverage.py reads measurements through the plain `location` column, not the annotation. The same shape holds in tests/test_core/test_project/test_models.py.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test where a measurement in a public dataset has no location of its own and its visible sample sits in another dataset at a point outside every other located record in the measurement's dataset: dataset.spatial_coverage() must include that point. It must go red when the pair reads `location` instead of `effective_location`.

findings.claim: The tests of the documented `declare_addressing` extension point were deleted with the location page, and the mechanism stays in the codebase with a documentation page, no caller and no test.
findings.evidence: tests/test_contrib/test_plugins/test_registration.py (TestARecordWithoutAUuid) and tests/test_contrib/test_plugins/test_menus.py (TestMenusExistForAnyRecord) removed; fairdm/contrib/plugins/registration.py:77 declare_addressing, route_for, lookup_for and get_addressing remain; docs/portal-development/create_a_plugin.md:317 documents `registry.declare_addressing(Station, route="<str:code>", lookup={"code": "code"})` as the way to address a record with no uuid. decisions.md D18 records that the machinery 'now has no test and no caller'. The tests' subject was the mechanism, not Point; Point was only its one instance. Reverse of a plugin URL by a non-uuid lookup, the ValueError for an uncaptured lookup name and the default menu for a model with no hand-written one now have no coverage.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-point the deleted tests at a small test-only model (a `Station` with a `code`) registered in the test module, keeping each assertion; or, if the maintainer wants the machinery gone, delete declare_addressing and its documentation section in this change. Do not leave a documented API with no test.

findings.claim: The breaking changes have no entry in the repository's migration guide, and the upgrade notes omit that a measurement type declaring its own `location`, `location_elevation` or `location_uncertainty` now fails to load.
findings.evidence: CONSTITUTION.md:70 and :205 require a migration guide with step-by-step instructions for breaking changes, and docs/more/migration-guides.md is where earlier breaking features put theirs (FS-024, identifier resolvers). The diff does not touch it. The upgrade instructions are the bullet list at docs/portal-development/locations.md:449-460 and the changelog. Measurement did not carry a `location` before this branch, so a portal measurement type with a `location` CharField or foreign key (a common name) now raises Django's FieldError for a local field clashing with a field of its concrete base. docs/adr/0032 ('A portal's own sample type cannot declare a field named location...'), docs/portal-development/special_fields.md and custom-samples.md name sample types only. Also unstated: a template that reads `{{ sample.location.latitude }}` now renders empty without an error, and `select_related("location")`, `autocomplete_fields = ["location"]` and a person form listing `location` raise at query, check or import time.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one section to docs/more/migration-guides.md with numbered steps: rename a clashing measurement or sample field before upgrading and migrate its data; search for `location.latitude`/`.longitude`, `location__x/__y/__crs`, `select_related('location')`, `autocomplete_fields`, `PointFactory`, `/location/` links and the three settings; run `migrate` and re-enter locations. Add measurement types to the ADR consequence and to special_fields.md.

findings.claim: Two pages the diff does not touch still say a sample's location is a record it links to or a foreign key that import checks.
findings.evidence: docs/overview/data_model.md:77: 'A location: If the sample has a known geographic origin, you can link it to a location record.' docs/portal-administration/managing-samples.md:441: 'Foreign key references exist (dataset, location)' under Import Validation. There is no location record to link to after this branch (ADR 0032), and the import validates four location columns instead (docs/portal-development/locations.md:298-337). The first is the page a new portal developer reads for the data model.
findings.suggested_fix: data_model.md: 'A location: the point where the sample was taken, with an optional elevation and uncertainty, held on the sample itself.' managing-samples.md: replace location in the foreign-key list and name the latitude and longitude columns under the field-validity line.

findings.claim: FR-025 ('MUST say which of the two it is') is checked through the template context's `source` value, not the rendered page, so a template that titles both cases the same still passes.
findings.evidence: tests/test_core/test_measurement/test_plugins.py TestOverviewLocation asserts response.context['effective_location'].source and the map's data-lon/data-lat, never what the card says. fairdm/core/measurement/templates/measurement/measurement_overview.html:150-156 holds the two titles.
findings.suggested_fix: Per the testing standard the copy itself gets no test, so record FR-025 as demonstrated by the context value, or assert a stable non-copy hook (a data attribute on the card carrying the source) set by the template. The mutation it must fail under: both branches rendering the same card.

findings.claim: Three import refusal cases assert only that some row failed, so removing the check that is supposed to refuse them leaves the test green.
findings.evidence: tests/test_contrib/test_import_export/test_resources.py `test_a_row_that_cannot_be_read_is_reported_and_not_saved`: the cases with value None (latitude without longitude; elevation with empty coordinates; negative uncertainty) skip the message assertion (`if value is not None`). Mutation: delete the `incomplete` branch in LocationField.compress; ('49.0', '') then fails inside parse_coordinate('') instead and the case still passes.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each None case the fragment its refusal message carries and assert it, so the test fails when the intended check is removed.

findings.claim: A coordinate smaller than 0.0001 degrees in magnitude is refused on import because it reaches the parser as scientific notation, so an exported file does not always re-import (AS 5.2).
findings.evidence: fairdm/contrib/location/resources.py:186-193 builds the coordinate text with str(value); str(5e-05) is '5e-05', which parse_coordinate refuses (letters in the text). Probe: a row with latitude 0.00001 and longitude 0.00005 comes back invalid with '“5e-05” is not a longitude the portal can read'. The export writes such a value as a float, so the same file is refused. The form is not affected: LocationWidget.decompress writes fixed-point text.
findings.suggested_fix: In set_location, pass floats to the parser as format(Decimal(repr(value)), 'f'), the conversion LocationWidget.decompress already uses, instead of str(value).

findings.claim: Measurement lookups take the viewer separately from visible_to(), so `Measurement.objects.visible_to(member).inside(area)` silently answers for a visitor, and the documentation says the lookups combine with visible_to in either order.
findings.evidence: fairdm/core/measurement/managers.py:77 and :103 default user=None. Probe: a public-dataset measurement placed only by a private sample the member may open: `visible_to(member).inside(area)` is False, `visible_to(member).inside(area, user=member)` is True. docs/portal-development/locations.md:157-158 says every lookup combines with visible_to() 'in either order' and the measurement section shows `user=` only without visible_to. The result under-reports, it does not leak.
findings.suggested_fix: State on the measurement lookups' section and docstrings that the viewer must be passed again when visible_to is used, with the combined call as the example.

findings.claim: The location widget writes the submitted reference-system text into a JavaScript string inside an Alpine x-data attribute without JavaScript escaping, so a submitted value containing a quote runs as script when the invalid form is shown again.
findings.evidence: fairdm/contrib/location/templates/location/widgets/location.html:39 `fairdmLocationInput('{{ parts.srid.value|default:'4326' }}', ...)`. HTML escaping turns the quote into ', which the browser decodes before Alpine evaluates the expression. Rendered with value `');alert(document.domain);//` the attribute decodes to `fairdmLocationInput('');alert(document.domain);//', 'id_location_systems')`. The value is only ever the user's own POST (the stored value is always 4326 and the POST needs the CSRF token), so this is self-XSS.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `{{ parts.srid.value|default:'4326'|escapejs }}` inside the string, or pass the value through a data attribute read by the script.

findings.claim: An import file with latitude and longitude columns only, and empty cells for a record that holds an elevation, refuses the row instead of clearing the location, though the page says an empty cell clears the value.
findings.evidence: fairdm/contrib/location/resources.py:172-200: set_location passes instance.location_elevation (still stored, since the file has no elevation column) into LocationField.compress with empty coordinates, which raises no_point. docs/portal-development/locations.md:336-337: 'a file with only some of them changes only those. An empty cell clears the value.' test_empty_cells_clear_the_location uses a row with all four columns present.
findings.suggested_fix: Either clear the elevation and uncertainty with the point when both coordinate cells are present and empty, as the form does, or add the exception to the documentation sentence.

findings.claim: The new dependency is an exact pin in a published package whose other dependencies use ranges.
findings.evidence: pyproject.toml:118 `"lat-lon-parser==1.3.1"`. Every neighbouring entry is a range (`pillow (>=11.0,<13.0)`, `gunicorn >=23.0.0,<27.0.0`). A portal that depends on another package needing a different lat-lon-parser cannot resolve. uv.lock is updated and matches.
findings.suggested_fix: `lat-lon-parser (>=1.3.1,<2.0)`, after reading its changelog for 1.x as the dependency discipline asks.

notes: docs/adr/0033 says the measurement lookups 'read' with_effective_location; inside() and within_distance() build their own two Sample.objects.visible_to() subqueries instead. Same rule, two code paths.
Spatial.polygon and Spatial.point set .srid on the caller's geometry in place when it has none.

SC-007 read literally (no document refers to Point, FAIRDM_CRS and the others): locations.md 'Upgrading', ADRs 0032 and 0033 and CONTEXT.md name them to say they are gone. decisions.md D15 excludes only the changelog.
demo/plugins.py still carries a module-docstring example registering a plugin on a `Location` model with .latitude, .longitude and .samples.all(), which describes the removed location page.

specs/030-geospatial-locations is tracked with brief-*.json, report-*.json, design-review-*.json and feature-state.json machine payloads (outside this diff's scope).
